justification: No clear etymology outside of Greek ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):34, [Beekes 2010](src-66):38-39}). It is likely that Ancient Greek αἷμα was a lexical replacement for the inherited word for 'blood', ἔαρ < *h₁esh₂-r̥- (cf. [cognate set 859](cog-859)), which was only retained as a poetic word in the language of Homeric epic and other archaic poetry.

gloss: take with the hand, take away
justification: Root etymology for the Hellenic lexemes in this class follows [LIV²](src-141) 535 as though from PIE *sr̥-i̯é- to PIE 3. *ser- 'to take, seize, grasp', but cf. [Frisk 1960-1972](src-174) I:43-44, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):38, [Beekes 2010](src-66):42 (without reference to new literature in [LIV²](src-141)).

Tocharian, Hellenic, Indo-Iranic, Baltic, Germanic, and Italic reflecting different derivatives from PIE *gʷerh₂- (cf. [Hilmarsson 1996](src-149):173-174, [Adams 2013](src-345):230-231, [Beekes 2010](src-66):202-203, [EWAia](src-172) I:490-491, [Turner 1962–1966](src-442):91 no.1962, [Karulis 1992](src-534) I:321, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):312, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):272, [Meyer-Lübke 1935](src-444):328 no. 3855).
Hellenic, Iranic, and Italic lexemes from PIE *mr̥g̑ʰ-ú- 'short' ([NIL](src-274) 497-499, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):236, [EWAia](src-172) II:364-365, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):75).

Etymology outside of Greek difficult; probably to IE *gres- (or *gras-) 'devour' (cf. [LIV²](src-141) 192, [IEW](src-49) 404) with dissimilation of *-r- in the root from the suffix *-tēr- (so [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):211-212); but cf. the objections of [Beekes 2010](src-66):262.

A unique Greco-Armenian isogloss ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):214, [Beekes 2010](src-66):264-265, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):336-337, 340-341, [LIV²](src-141) 162; cf. [Clackson 1994](src-319):126-131 for extensive discussion of the various reflexes and derivatives from this root).

gloss: sweet to the taste or smell
justification: Very similar in form and meaning to Latin dulcis 'sweet', but a common proto-form cannot be reconstructed. Perhaps the Italic and Greek lexemes are independent borrowings from a third source (cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):228-229, [Beekes 2010](src-66):227-228). Cf. further discussion in [cognate set 7772](cog-7772).

Within Hellenic the root of the noun, *γλῶχ- / *glōkʰ 'point', is attested via γλωχίς 'end of a yoke strap, barb of an arrow, etc.', but there are no known cognates outside of Greek ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):229-230, [Beekes 2010](src-66):278).

Anatolian, Tocharian, Hellenic, Armenian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Germanic, and Celtic lexemes from PIE *gʷen- 'woman' ([NIL](src-274) 177-185, cf. [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):501-505, [Hilmarsson 1996](src-149):157-159, [Adams 2013](src-345):242, [Beekes 2010](src-66):291-292, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79)363-364, [EWAia](src-172) I:568-569, [Derksen 2015](src-353):558, [Derksen 2008](src-81):558, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):317, [Matasović 2009](src-50):61).

Anatolian, Tocharian, Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *g̑enu, *g̑neu- ([IEW](src-49) 381-382, cf. [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):467-468, [Hilmarsson 1996](src-149):129-130, [Adams 2013](src-345):205-206, [Beekes 2010](src-66):283, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):343-344, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):190-191, [Orel 1998](src-105):137, [EWAia](src-172): I:584-585, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):296, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):259, [Matasović 2009](src-50):162). NB: traditionally considered a separate lexical root from PIE 2. *g̑enu- 'jaw, chin' (cf. [IEW](src-49) 380-382).
No certain etymology outside of Greek ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):218-219, [Beekes 2010](src-66):269-270).

Greek and Indic lexemes derived from PIE *denk̑- 'to bite' ([LIV²](src-141) 117-118, [EWAia](src-172) I:688, [Beekes 2010](src-66):299). Sometimes connected to these lexemes are also  Tocharian AB tsāk- 'to bite', but these lexemes are probably better explained via PIE *dʰei̯Hgʷ- 'to sting' (cf. [LIV²](src-141) 142, [Ringe 1988-1990](src-592):71).

Anatolian, Hellenic, Albanian, Iranic, Slavic, and Germanic lexemes derived from PIE *déru- ~ *dóru- ~ *dru- 'wood, tree' ([Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):849-850, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):262-263, [Beekes 2010](src-66):315-316, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):146-148, [Orel 1998](src-105):76, [EWAia](src-172) I:721, [ESIJa](src-331) 2:357-365, [ESSJa](src-458) 4:211-213, [Derksen 2008](src-81):99, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):522-523, cf. [IEW](src-49) 214-217).

Hellenic lexemes from PIE *dér-mn̥ '(flayed) skin, leather' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):265-266, [Beekes 2010](src-66):318; a derivative of PIE *der- 'to tear (intr.), split' cf. [LIV²](src-141) 119-121).
Hellenic lexemes from PIE *deh₁- 'to bind' ([Beekes 2010](src-66):321-322, [LIV²](src-141) 102, cf. [Babinotis 2010](src-382):338).

Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *deh₃- 'to give' ([LIV²](src-141) 105-106, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):331-332, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):595, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):154-155, [Orel 1998](src-105):157, [Rohr 2000](src-687):42-43, [EWAia](src-172) I:713-715, [Turner 1962–1966](src-442):489 no. 8655, [Cheung 2007](src-83):45-47, [ALEW](src-352) 246-248, [Derksen 2015](src-353):146-147, [ESSJa](src-458) 4:194-195, [Derksen 2008](src-81):96, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):174-175). The connection of Gaulish dede to this class is tentatively accepted (so [Matasović 2009](src-50):86), but cf. the discussion of [Delamarre 2003](src-157):138-139 regarding the possibility alternatively deriving the Gaulish form from PIE *dʰeh₁- 'to put, place'.

In spite of numerous phonological and morphological difficulties, often assumed to be root-cognate with Latin lācrima 'tear', Armenian artaswr 'tear', OHG zahar 'tear', Ved. áśru-, TochA ākär, Hittite išḫaḫru 'tear(s)', etc., (cf. [Hamp 1972](src-575)). The Leiden dictionaries (cf. [de Vaan 2008](src-54):322, [Beekes 2010](src-66):299-300) generally follow the proposal of [Kortlandt 1985a](src-574), assuming a common pre-form for the Greek and Latin forms as a nominal compound *dr̥k̑-h₂k̑ru- 'eye-bitter' containing the roots *derk̑- 'catch sight of, look at' and *h₂ek̑- 'be sharp'.

Hellenic, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes reflecting different derivations from PIE *dek̑s- 'to be suitable' ([Beekes 2010](src-66):316-317, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):137-138, [Orel 1998](src-105):67-68, [EWAia](src-172) I:690-691, [Turner 1962–1966](src-442):349 no. 6119, [ALEW](src-352) 199, [Derksen 2015](src-353):124, [ESSJa](src-458) 4:218-219, [Derksen 2008](src-81):100-101, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):512, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):168, {Matasović 2009}:97, cf. [LIV²](src-141) 112)

Anatolian, Tocharian, Greek, and Armenian lexemes derived from PIE *sem- 'one (collective)' ([LIPP 2](src-294):671-679, cf. [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):750-751, [Adams 2013](src-345):721-722, [Beekes 2010](src-66):394, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):467-468).
No satisfactory etymology outside of Greek; for some proposed inner-Greek connections cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):384-385, [Beekes 2010](src-66):479.

Hellenic, Indo-Iranic, and Italic lexemes from PIE *h₁urH-ú- 'broad, wide', presupposing a full-grade root *h₁u̯erH- (cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):483-484, [EWAia](src-172) I:227, [Abaev 1959–1995](src-156) IV:90-91, [Untermann 2000](src-279):310, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):645).

Tocharian, Greek, Armenian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *gʷi̯eh₃- 'to live' ([LIV²](src-141) 215-216, cf. [Adams 2013](src-345):683-684, [Beekes 2010](src-66):505, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):356-357, [EWAia](src-172) I:594, [Cheung 2007](src-83):222-223, [ALEW](src-352) 338-340, [Derksen 2008](src-81):652, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):685-686, [Matasović 2009](src-50):67).

Of obscure origin, probably a prehistoric loanword (cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):420, [Beekes 2010](src-66):530 for discussion of various hypotheses). The different dialectal forms point to either a Proto-Greek or borrowed source form *tʰalak⁽ʰ⁾i̯a (vel sim.).

Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, Iranic, and Germanic lexemes derived from PIE *gʷʰer- 'to become warm' ([NIL](src-274) 196-199, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):541-542, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):556-557, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):298, [Orel 1998](src-105):303, 525, [EWAia](src-172) I:513, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):575). Most lexemes in this class (Greek, Armenian, Iranic, Germanic) reflect a PIE adjectival stem *gʷʰer-mó-. Albanian is only root-cognate with the rest of the forms and has a distinct stem formation (cf. [Demiraj 1997](src-369):298 for further discussion).
Greek θηρεύω is a secondary formation to an old IE root noun *g̑ʰu̯eh₁r- 'wild animal' (> AGk. θήρ) ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):435-436, [Beekes 2010](src-66):547).

Stem alternation between, e.g., nominative singular θρίξ, genitive singular τριχός due to Graßmann's Law point to a Proto-Greek stem *tʰrikʰ-, but further connections outside of Greek are unclear ([Frisk 1960-1972](src-174) I:684, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):441-442, [Beekes 2010](src-66):556).

Anatolian, Hellenic, and Indo-Iranic lexemes reflecting an original athematic root-present to PIE *h₁eh₁s- 'to sit' ([LIV²](src-141) 232, [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):252-255, [Beekes 2010](src-66):518, [EWAia](src-172) I:181).

Anatolian, Tocharian, Hellenic, Indo-Iranic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from a basic PIE root *k̑er- (cf. [Nussbaum 1986](src-544) for extensive discussion of formations in the meaning 'head' and 'horn' derived from this root). Cf. also [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):456-457, [Adams 2013](src-345):235 [but cf. [Hilmarsson 1996](src-149):182 deriving to *gʰreh₁-u̯r̥], [Beekes 2010](src-66):676-677, [EWAia](src-172) II:653, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):259, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):136-137, [Matasović 2009](src-50):190-191).
No known etymology outside of Greek ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):519-520, [Beekes 2010](src-66):679).

Hellenic lexemes derived from PIE *k̑eh₂u̯- 'to kindle; to burn' ([LIV²](src-141) 345, [Beekes 2010](src-66):618, cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):480-481). For the root reconstruction with initial palatovelar *k̑- (rather than plain velar *k-) cf. [LIV² Addenda \& Corrigenda](src-389).
No consensus etymology; cf. [Frisk 1960-1972](src-174):585, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):384, and [Beekes 2010](src-66):478 for various proposals.

Possibly to be connected with Proto-Albanian *kakii̯ā̆- (cf. [Schumacher & Matzinger 2013](src-364):239), but it is difficult to be fully certain of the etymology (cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):619-620. Cf. further in [cognate set 6597](cog-6597).

Possibly to IE *kʷu̯ap- (or less likely *kʷu̯eh₂p-) if to be compared with Lat. vapor 'steam, exhalation', Lith. kvė̃pti 'breathe' ([ALEW](src-352) 545-546, [Derksen 2015](src-353):268), but these connections are not fully certain due to several irregular sound-changes needed to justify the comparison (cf. Chantraine 1968–1980}:494-495, [Beekes 2010](src-66):638-639).

Anatolian, Hellenic, Armenian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes from PIE *k̑erd- 'heart' ([NIL](src-274) 417-423, cf. [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):469-471, [Beekes 2010](src-66):644, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):576-578, [EWAia](src-172) II:818, [ALEW](src-352) 1032-1034, [Derksen 2015](src-353):448-449, [Derksen 2008](src-81):485, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):134-135, [Matasović 2009](src-50):223-224). The irregular correspondence of Proto-Indo-Iranic word-initial *j́ʰ- (> Ved. h-, Av. z-) is presumably due to contamination with Proto-Indo-Iranic outcome of PIE *g̑ʰórh₁-/g̑ʰr̥h₁- 'guts', cf. cognate set 2672.

Root ref. form follows [LIV²](src-141) 559; cf. also [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):200, [Beekes 2010](src-66):649, and [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):452-453 (s.v. Hitt. karp(ii̯e/a)- 'to take (away), take up, lift, pluck').

Hellenic lexemes from a PIE stem *gʰebʰh₂l-. A reconstruction with a laryngeal *-h₂- is required because of the connection with Tocharian AB śpāl 'head'; also connected with OHG gebal 'skull' (cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):522, [Beekes 2010](src-66):682-683, [Adams 2013](src-345):703).
Hellenic lexemes derived from PIE *kreu̯h₂- '(clotted) blood, blood outside of the body, gore' ([NIL](src-274) 444-448, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):580, [Beekes 2010](src-66):774).

No precise correspondences outside of Greek ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):589, [Beekes 2010](src-66):786-787). The closest possible correspondences are in Balto-Slavic (cf. OCS kryti 'hide', Lith. kráuti 'heap' in [cognate set 5275](cog-5275)), but the connection is uncertain.

Generally considered a derivative of Ancient Greek κρύος 'cold' in the older literature (cf. [Frisk 1960-1972](src-174) II:28-29, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):588-589), although the stem-formation is obscure. [Beekes 2010](src-66):787 therefore has rejected the older proposed etymology in favour of assuming a substratum borrowing from a 'Pre-Greek' language. A third possibility is that there has been some degree of contamination or blending of the lexical root underlying Ancient Greek κρύος with some other (substratum?) lexical material (cf. note by Scarborough in this class), although this too is a speculative solution.

Hellenic lexemes as though from PIE *ken(H)-is- ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):562, [Beekes 2010](src-66):746-747, [Babinotis 2010](src-382):706, 1284, cf. [de Vaan 2008](src-54):115). The connection of Albanian hi 'ash' to this class (cf. [cognate set 850](cog-850)) presupposes the reconstruction of an s-mobile root *(s)ken(H)- (cf. [Huld 1984](src-571):74, [Orel 1998](src-105):47).

Hellenic lexemes in the meaning 'round' as a derived relational adjective from Ancient Greek κύκλος 'circle, ring, wheel' < PIE *kʷe-kʷl-o- 'circle; wheel', a derivative to PIE *kʷelh₁- 'to turn' ([Beekes 2010](src-66):798-799, cf. [LIV²](src-141) 386-388).

Anatolian, Tocharian, Hellenic, Armenian, Indo-Iranic, Baltic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes continuing PIE *k̑u̯ón-, *k̑un-, *k̑u̯n̥-, the inherited Indo-European word for 'dog' ([NIL](src-274) 436-440, [EIEC](src-657) 168, cf. [Melchert 1989](src-692), [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):505-506, [Hilmarsson 1996](src-149):187, [Adams 2013](src-345):190, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):520-522, Beekes 2010}:811, [EWAia](src-172) II:674-675, [ALEW](src-352) 1054-1055, [Derksen 2015](src-353):455, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):256, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):87, [Matasović 2009](src-50):181).
Hellenic lexemes derived from PIE *leg̑- 'to collect, to pick up' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):625-626, [Beekes 2010](src-66):841-842, [LIV²](src-141) 397).
No certain etymology outside of Greek (cf. [Frisk 1960-1972](src-174) II:122, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):640, [Beekes 2010](src-66):861).

Tocharian and Hellenic lexemes derived from PIE *lei̯- ([Beekes 2010](src-66):843-844, [Adams 2013](src-345):614). The Tocharian lexemes are generally considered to be based on an *mn-stem neuter to an IE root *lei̯- ([Ringe 1996](src-695):109, [Adams 2013](src-345):614), and connected to the complex of words surrounding Gk. λειμών 'wet, grassy place, meadow' λίμην 'harbour', and λίμνη 'lake', but cf. [van Windekens 1976](src-76):271-272 for older hypotheses.
Hellenic lexemes derived from PIE *leu̯k- 'to become bright' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):632-633, [Beekes 2010](src-66):851, cf. [LIV²](src-141) 418-419).

Hellenic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes traditionally reconciled to a basic root *lei̯- 'smooth', although the Celtic forms here may also require s-mobile (cf. ([IEW](src-49) 662-664, [Falileyev 2000](src-240):103, [Matasović 2009](src-50):346, [Beekes 2010](src-66):844, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):336-337). The Germanic forms derived from PIE *slei̯g̑- 'smear, make smooth' in [cognate set 8680](cog-8680) might be an extended form of this root. See further discussion in that cognate class.

No consensus etymology outside of Greek (cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):673-674, [Beekes 2010](src-66):916-917); [Malzahn & Peters 2010](src-648) propose a connection to Tocharian B mäk- 'run', but the meanings are divergent (cf. 'run' in [cognate set 7203](cog-7203)). [LIV²](src-141) 422 assigns to *magʰ- 'to be able'.

Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *meg̑- 'big' ([NIL](src-274) 468-478, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):917-918, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):458-460, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):250-251, [Orel 1998](src-105):240, [EWAia](src-172) II:337-338, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):361-362, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):358-359, [Matasović 2009](src-50):253). For Tocharian lexemes not in the target meaning attached to this class, cf. [Adams 2013](src-345):479-480.

Hellenic and Baltic lexemes generally connected with Indic lexemes in the meaning 'dirty' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):680-681, [Beekes 2010](src-66):923-924; cf. [Derksen 2015](src-353):554, [EWAia](src-172) II:332-333).

Hellenic lexemes from a zero-grade derivative *mh₂k̑-ró-, derived from PIE *meh₂k̑- 'long, thin, tall' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):660-661, [Beekes 2010](src-66):895, [NIL](src-274) 478-481, cf. [Babinotis 2010](src-382):810).
Hellenic lexemes from PIE *mē(m)s- 'meat' ([NIL](src-274) 486-488, [Beekes 2010](src-66):947).
Without clear correspondences outside of Greek ([Frisk 1960-1972](src-174) II:236-237, [Beekes 2010](src-66):951-952).

Many irregular developments, often assumed to be due to taboo deformation, but all the lexemes are generally assumed to come from a common Indo-European source. The metathesised stem *u̯orm- as found in Vedic, etc. is generally assumed to be a taboo-deformation while the forms found in Avestan maoiri-, Old Irish moirb are often assumed to be most closely reflect to the original ([EIEC](src-657) 24). For individual branches, cf. [Adams 2013](src-345):630, [Beekes 2010](src-66):982, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):482-483, [EWAia](src-172) II:507, [ESSJa](src-458) 19:241-249, [Derksen 2008](src-81):326, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):359, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):243, [Matasović 2009](src-50):278.

Hellenic, Albanian, Balto-Slavic, and Italic lexemes derived from PIE *mus- 'fly, gnat', cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):976, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):270, [Orel 1998](src-105):268, [ALEW](src-352) 673-674, [Derksen 2015](src-353):326, [ESSJa](src-458) 20:170-172, [Derksen 2008](src-81):330-331, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):397).

Anatolian, Tocharian, Hellenic, Armenian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *neu̯- 'new' ([NIL](src-274) 524-526, cf. [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):605, [Adams 2013](src-345):287-288, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1009, [Hübschmann 1897](src-564):479, [EWAia](src-172) II:25, [ALEW](src-352) 690-691, [Derksen 2015](src-353):330-331, [ESSJa](src-458) 26:9-13, [Derksen 2008](src-81):357, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):389, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):416, {ref Matasović 2009:293). Not the same root as PIE *neu̯- 'to nod, tilt (the head)' (cf. [LIV²](src-141) 455-456)

Hellenic, Armenian, Indo-Iranic, and Baltic derivatives from PIE *nebʰ- 'become damp, cloudy, misty' ([NIL](src-274) 499-504). Cf. also [ALEW](src-352) 186-187, [Derksen 2015](src-353):118, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1012, [EWAia](src-172) I:94, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):49-51).

Tocharian, Hellenic, Indo-Iranic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *(s)neh₂- 'to bathe, swim' ([LIV²](src-141) 572-573; cf. [Adams 2013](src-345):354-355, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1012-1013, [EWAia](src-172) II:769-770, [Turner 1962–1966](src-442):39, [Cheung 2007](src-83):348-349, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):411, [Matasović 2009](src-50):348).

Hellenic, Indo-Iranic, and Celtic lexemes from PIE *nei̯gʷ- 'to wash' ([LIV²](src-141) 450, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):1020-1021, [EWAia](src-172) II:54, [Turner 1962–1966](src-442):410 no. 7167, [Vendryes et al. 1959–1996](src-296) N:16-17, [Matasović 2009](src-50):290-291).

Hellenic, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Germanic, Italic and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *nógʷt-/*négʷt- 'evening, night', a dental-stem derivative of PIE *negʷ- 'to become dark, dawn' ([NIL](src-274) 504-513, [LIV²](src-141) 449, cf. {ref {Beekes 2010}:1027, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):283-284, [Orel 1998](src-105):282-283, [EWAia](src-172) II:2-3, [Steblin-Kamenskij 1999](src-321):242, [ALEW](src-352) 683-684, [Derksen 2015](src-353):327-328, [ESSJa](src-458) 25:175-177, [Derksen 2008](src-81):355, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):381, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):416-417, [Matasović 2009](src-50):293-294). The Brythonic lexemes in this class are sometimes considered to be (parallel?) loanwords from Latin (cf. [Matasović 2009](src-50):293-294, [Deshayes 2003](src-309):539-540), but by others to be inherited (cf. [Geiriadur Prifysgol Cymru (GPC)](src-236), [Falileyev 2000](src-240):121, [NIL](src-274) 509n10). The assumption that these lexemes are inherited has been followed here.
No certain etymology outside of Greek (cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):762, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1031).
Etymology outside of Greek uncertain ([Frisk 1960-1972](src-174): II:333, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):763-764, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1033).

Connections outside of Greek unclear; occasionally proposed to Arm. čʻor 'dry' (cf. [cognate set 5006](cog-5006)), but this requires postulating a sound law in Armenian for which this is the only example (cf. [Clackson 1994](src-319):182, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1035-1036, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):546).

Greek and Armenian lexemes derived from PIE *h₂ei̯d- 'to swell' ([LIV²](src-141) 258-259, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1053-1054, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):61). Albanian forms in [cognate set 8292](cog-8292) might be cognate to this set but ultimately uncertain, cf. discussion in that cognate class.
Hellenic and Indo-Iranic lexemes derived from PIE *u̯ei̯k̑-/*u̯oi̯k̑- 'house' ([Beekes 2010](src-66):1055-1056, [EWAia](src-172) II:584-585, cf. [LIV²](src-141) 669-670).

Etymology outside of Greek unknown, possibly to PIE *h₂eu̯- 'to perceive' if a de-adverbial formation as though from *h₂ou̯is-i̯é- ([Beekes 2010](src-66):1059-1060, cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):785-786).

Hellenic, Armenian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Germanic, and Celtic lexemes from the perfect stem *u̯oi̯d- 'to know' (< *'to have seen') from PIE *u̯ei̯d- 'to catch sight of' ([LIV²](src-141) 665-667, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):1053, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):211, [EWAia](src-172) II:579-581, [Cheung 2007](src-83):408-409, [Derksen 2015](src-353):566, [Derksen 2008](src-81):518), Matasović 2009}:422-423).
Greek and Celtic lexemes as nominal derivatives of PIE *h₁ers- 'rear' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):838, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1127-1128, [Matasović 2009](src-50):118).

The best IE etymology, is a derivation to *h₂u̯ers- 'rain' (so [Wackernagel 1888](src-670):129 = Kl.Schr. 1.632, tentatively accepted by [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):838-839, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1128). The hypothesis of substrate borrowing is a possibility but, given that there is no concrete extra-Greek comparison for it, gratuitous. For the purposes of cognacy Wackernagel's etymology has been followed here.

Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, Balto-Slavic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *h₂ou̯s-os-, *h₂au̯s-os-, *h₂us-es- 'ear' ([NIL](src-274) 339-343, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):1130-1131, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):637-638, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):415, [Orel 1998](src-105):501, [ALEW](src-352) 74, [Derksen 2015](src-353):71, [Derksen 2008](src-81):507, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):63, [Matasović 2009](src-50):48-49).

Tocharian, Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes continuing PIE *pénkʷe 'five', generally considered to be the Indo-European inherited numeral for 'five' (not attested in phonetic spellings in Anatolian languages). See [Eichner 1982](src-342):383-569 for extensive discussion, cf. also [Adams 2013](src-345):415-416, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1172-1173, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):409, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):315-316, [Orel 1998](src-105):316, [EWAia](src-172) II:65-66, [ALEW](src-352) 756-767, [Derksen 2015](src-353):351, [Derksen 2008](src-81):400, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):140, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):509, [Matasović 2009](src-50):176-177.

Anatolian, Hellenic, Indo-Iranic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *pet- 'to fly, fall' ([LIV² Addenda \& Corrigenda](src-389); cf. [LIV²](src-141) 476, [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):655-660, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1181-1182, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):286-287, 294, [EWAia](src-172) II:71-72, [Matasović 2009](src-50):129)
Hellenic lexemes derived from PIE *peh₂g̑- 'become firm' (cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):894-895, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1184, [LIV²](src-141) 461).

Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *peh₃(i̯)- 'to drink' ([LIV²](src-141) 262, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):1194-1195, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):277-279, [Orel 1998](src-105):324-325, [Schumacher & Matzinger 2013](src-364):990, [EWAia](src-172) II:113-114, [Derksen 2015](src-353):563, [Derksen 2008](src-81):401, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):71-72, [Matasović 2009](src-50):130).

Hellenic and Indo-Iranic lexemes derived traditionally assigned to a root *peth₁- 'to fall' ([LIV²](src-141) 477-478, cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):905-906, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1195-1196). See now [LIV² Addenda \& Corrigenda](src-389) considering a more basic PIE root *pet- 'to fall; to fly' merging also 2. *peth₂- 'to fly' ([LIV²](src-141) 479). Cf. also [EWAia](src-172) II:71-72).

gloss: play (like a child), sport, dance, play (a game)
justification: A denominal verb from Ancient Greek παῖς (gen. παιδός) 'child', cf. cognate set 1462 for further discussion.

Hellenic lexemes derived from the adverb πάλαι, probably a fossilised case form of a root noun *pl̥h₂-ei̯ and to be connected with πέλας 'near', πελάζω 'approach, draw near', πίλναμαι 'draw near, approach', πλησίον 'near' (adv.) from *pelh₂-, in the sense *'in the (near, recent) past' > 'old' ([Chadwick 1976](src-718), [Beekes 2010](src-66):1144-1145). Older etymologies attempting to connect to the same root as Att. τῆλε 'far away' (cf. Aeol. πήλυι) cannot be correct since Mycenaean pa-ra-jo does not contain a labiovelar as one would expect ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):851, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1144-1145).

Hellenic, Indo-Iranic, and Baltic lexemes derived from PIE *bʰeng̑ʰ- ([NIL](src-274) 13-15, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):1159-1160, [EWAia](src-172) II:220-221, [Turner 1962–1966](src-442):518, [ALEW](src-352) 115-116).
Hellenic lexemes from PIE *pik̑-ro-, a derivative to PIE *pei̯k̑- 'to cut out, carve out' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):900-901, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1190, cf. [LIV²](src-141) 465-466).

Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *pleh₁- 'to fill, be(come) full' ([Beekes 2010](src-66):1191-1192, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):309-310, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):327, [Orel 1998](src-105):335, [EWAia](src-172) II:156-157, [ALEW](src-352) 772-773, [Derksen 2015](src-353):356, [Derksen 2008](src-81):426, [Kroonen 2013](src-165)159, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):472-273, [Matasović 2009](src-50):132).

Hellenic lexemes of uncertain etymology, perhaps from a PIE root *pneu̯- if cognate with Germanic lexemes attested by, e.g., Old Norse fnýsa 'sniff, snort' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):920, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1213-1214, [LIV²](src-141) 489).

Hellenic lexemes whose root etymology is traditionally disputed between the near-homophonous roots *peth₁- 'to fall', 1. *peth₂- 'to spread out', and 2. *peth₂- 'to fly' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):931, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1225-1226, cf. [LIV²](src-141) 477-479). See now, however, [LIV² Addenda \& Corrigenda](src-389) merging *peth₁- 'to fall' and 2. *peth₂- 'to fly' into a single, more basic root *pet- 'to fly; to fall'. In view of this, the basic etymology to *pet- has been tentatively accepted here.

Anatolian, Tocharian, Hellenic, Armenian, Indo-Iranic, Germanic, and Italic lexemes derived from PIE *ped- 'to step; to fall, sink' ([NIL](src-274) 526-540), cf. [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):653-654, [Adams 2013](src-345):432, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1227-1228, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):534-535, [EWAia](src-172) II:77-78 [Kroonen 2013](src-165):152, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):462, [LIV²](src-141) 458).

gloss: do, be busy with; accomplish; manage affairs
justification: Often connected with the family of Ancient Greek πείρω 'pierce, run through' (cf. [LIV²](src-141) 472-473 s.v. 1. *per- 'hindurchkommen, durchqueren') with a velar extension to the root, but the root and stem formation remains nonetheless obscure (cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):934-935, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1229-1230).

Anatolian, Hellenic, Armenian, Nuristani, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *pet- 'to fly, to fall'. For the root reconstruction cf. [LIV² Addenda \& Corrigenda](src-389). For individual branches cf. [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):658-659, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1248, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):286-287, {Turner 1962–1966}:437 no. 7733, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):138-139, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):458, [Matasović 2009](src-50):126).

Anatolian, Hellenic, Armenian, Indo-Iranic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *pet- 'to fly, fall' ([Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):658-659, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1248, [EWAia](src-172) II:75-76, [Turner 1962–1966](src-442):435-436 no.7721, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):138-139, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):458, [Lucht 2007](src-151):151-152, [Matasović 2009](src-50):129). For the root reconstruction *pet-, cf. [LIV² Addenda \& Corrigenda](src-389).
Hellenic lexemes continuing PIE *poi̯H-u̯eh₂- 'grass, meadow', cf. Lithuanian píeva 'meadow' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):922, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1214-1215, cf. [ALEW](src-352) 769).

Two possible etymologies: Either identical to Lat. porrō 'forward' if from *p(o)rsōd, alternatively from *πόρσω, derived from πρός 'towards' (< PIE *próti) with a commonly found liquid metathesis. Since both derivations have similar semantic paths of derivation it is difficult to choose between the two possibilities ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):929, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1223).

Anatolian, Tocharian, Hellenic, Armenian, Baltic, Germanic, and Sabellic lexemes derived from PIE *péh₂-u̯r̥, *ph₂-u̯én-, an inherited r/n-heteroclitic nominal stem (cf. [NIL](src-274) 540-545, [EIEC](src-657) 202, cf. [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):613-614, [Adams 2013](src-345):421-422, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1260-1261, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):426-427, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):151, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):500).
Internal reconstruction points to a root *tu̯eh₂p-, *ti̯eh₂p- or *⁽k̑⁾i̯eh₂p- ([LIV²](src-141) 361 reconstructs *Ki̯eh₂p-), but no cognates are known outside of Greek ([Beekes 2010](src-66):1324).

Hellenic lexemes, originally from a derived adjective in *-nā to Ancient Greek σέλας 'light, brightness', i.e. Proto-Greek *selásnā- (cf. Lesbian σέλαννα 'moon'). Further etymology obscure ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):955, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1318-1319).

The root etymology in this set follows [LIV²](src-141) 549 and the latter of the two possible etymologies suggested by [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1011 to a PIE root *skabʰ- 'to scratch, shave'. Cf. however [Beekes 2010](src-66):1342-1343 favouring a substrate origin.
Hellenic lexemes derived from PIE *skel- 'bend, curve' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1013, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1346).

Tocharian, Hellenic, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, and Slavic lexemes continuing derivatives of a PIE root *s⁽k̑⁾eH- where the indeterminate laryngeal is probably *-h₂- on the basis of Ancient Greek σκηνή (West Greek σκᾱνᾱ́) 'tent' < *'cloth to provide shade' < *s⁽k̑⁾eh₂-néh₂ ([Beekes 2010](src-66):1350-1351). Also attested in Greek is σκότος 'darkness, gloom' which must formally continue *s⁽k̑⁾h₃-to- ([Beekes 2010](src-66):1359-1360). It is probably best to separate these as distinct roots, although formally they may well be (sandhi?) variants of one another at the PIE level. For further discussion cf. [Adams 2013](src-345):773, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1350-1351, [Andriotis 1974](src-460):498, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):201, [Orel 1998](src-105):147-148, [EWAia](src-172) I:559-560, [Turner 1962–1966](src-442):275-276 no. 5027, [Derksen 2008](src-81):447).

Hellenic lexemes as though from PIE *skl̥h₁-ró-, an derived adjective to PIE *(s)kelh₁- 'to dry out, dry up' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1012-1013, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1345-1346, cf. [LIV²](src-141) 553).
Etymology outside Hellenic uncertain ({ref Chantraine {1968–1980}:1025-1026, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1364).

Hellenic and Albanian lexemes derived from PIE *sper- 'to spread, scatter' ([LIV²](src-141) 580). The connection of Albanian lexemes to this class follows [Demiraj 1997](src-369):56, [Orel 1998](src-105):93, but more skeptically cf. [Holm 2011](src-130):78; for Hellenic, cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1035-1036, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1379-1380, [Babinotis 2010](src-382):1316).

Variants among the Ancient Greek dialects point to an original u-stem *stenu- that was later thematised as *stenu̯o- (with subsequent loss of medial *-u̯-), but further connections outside of Greek remain unclear ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1051-1052, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1399).

Hellenic lexemes from PIE *stéh₃-mn, *sth₃-mén-s, cf. Hitt. ištāman- 'ear', Av. staman- 'snout, maw' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1058-1059, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1408, cf. [Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):411-413).

The connection of the forms in this class to those from PIE *pstḗn in [cognate set 2217](cog-2217) is disputed, and rest on assuming that it is root-cognate with a gloss στήνιον from Hesychius's Lexicon. The word-formation within Greek is, however, unclear ([Frisk 1960-1972](src-174) II:795, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1054-1055, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1403-1404, cf. [IEW](src-49) 990).

The reflexes found in the individual languages reflect different generalised accent/ablaut classes of PIE *kʷetu̯or-, *kʷ(e)tu̯r̥-, *kʷ(e)tur- 'four'. For extensive discussion cf. [Eichner 1982](src-342):298-382, cf. also [Adams 2013](src-345):703, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1471-1472, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):546-547, [Orel 1998](src-105):173-174, [EWAia](src-172) I:526-527, [ALEW](src-352) 483-485, [Derksen 2015](src-353):241, [ESSJa](src-458) 4:97-98, [Derksen 2008](src-81):87, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):133, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):505-506, [Matasović 2009](src-50):179.
Hellenic lexemes as nominal derivatives PIE *dʰegʷʰ-r-h₂ from PIE *dʰegʷʰ- 'burn' ([Beekes 2010](src-66):1475-1476, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1112; cf. [LIV²](src-141) 133-134).

Hellenic lexemes traditionally considered a derivation to the same root as Ancient Greek τρέχω 'to run' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1130), but cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):1501 considering this explanation semantically unconvincing, with aspects of the word formation also unclear from an IE point of view.
IE root etymology difficult. This class tentatively follows [Beekes 2010](src-66):1503-1504, [LIV²](src-141) 650 s.v. *trep-, but cf. also [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1132-1133.
Hellenic lexemes from PIE *dʰre⁽g̑⁾ʰ- ([Beekes 2010](src-66):1506-1507, [LIV²](src-141) 154). For the Tsakonian lexemes in this class, cf. [Andriotis 1974](src-460):556-557.

The cognacy in this class follows [LIV²](src-141) to PIE *(s)teup- after [Oettinger 1979](src-649):417, 535, [Hajnal 1995](src-380):127. Note however disagreement of [Melchert 1994](src-368):242, [Neumann 2007](src-414):384-385, comparing Gk. στυφελίζω suggesting a root-variant *(s)teubʰ- (after [IEW](src-49) 1034; not in [LIV²](src-141)). According to [Beekes 2010](src-66):1418-1419, however, Gk. στυφελίζω has no secure connections outside of Greek.

Tocharian, Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *bʰer- 'to carry' ([LIV²](src-141) 76-77, cf. [Adams 2013](src-345):397-398, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1562-1564, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):176, [Schumacher & Matzinger 2013](src-364):965, [EWAia](src-172) I:246-249, [Cheung 2007](src-83):6-10, [Seebold 1970](src-556):104-106, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):59, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):213-214, [Matasović 2009](src-50):62).

Hellenic lexemes to be derived from the same root as Ancient Greek φθείρω 'to ruin, destroy' < *dʰgʷʰer-i̯e/o- 'flow away, disappear' ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1198, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1569). The onset cluster ψ- found in some Modern Greek dialects has probably come about via contamination with Modern Greek ψύλλα 'flea' ([Babinotis 2010](src-382):1626).

Etymology outside of Hellenic uncertain, possibly to be connected with verbs φλέω 'to teem with abundance, abound' and φλύω 'to boil over, bubble up' as derivatives of PIE *bʰleu̯H- 'to overflow'; cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1214, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1580, [Babinotis 2010](src-382):1546-1547.

Hellenic lexemes derived from PIE *bʰegʷ- 'to run away, flee' via the causative-iterative stem *bʰogʷ-éi̯e- 'to make run, flee' (cf. [LIV²](src-141) 67, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1183-1184, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1559).

The Tocharian, Hellenic, and Germanic lexemes in this class are generally considered derivations from PIE *bʰleh₃- 'to bloom', although certain derivational details remain disputed. Root ref. form follows [LIV²](src-141) 88, cf. [Adams 2013](src-345):415, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1232-1233, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1596-1597, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):66). It is possible, but uncertain that Latin folium and the Romance lexemes continuing it belong here, cf. further discussion in [cognate set 8247](cog-8247).

Anatolian, Tocharian, Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, and Indo-Iranic lexemes from PIE *g̑ʰes- *'grasp'(?), 'hand', 'grip' ([NIL](src-274) 170-173). Indo-Iranic cognates reflect *g̑ʰes-to- (cf. [EWAia](src-172) II:812), other languages reflect an r-stem g̑ʰes-r- or thematised r-stem *g̑ʰes-r-o- ([Kloekhorst 2008](src-80):471-472, [Adams 2013](src-345):711-712, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1620-1621, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):431-432, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):140, [Orel 1998](src-105):70).

Cf. [LIPP 2](src-294) s.v. *g̑ʰés- 'gestern' for extensive discussion of the attempted reconstructions of forms in this class, also [NIL](src-274) s.v. *dei̯-, *di- under ?*(g̑ʰ)-di-es (with discussion in footnotes 6-18). The cognacy of the lexemes in this class is not disputed, however there remains much disagreement in the literature how the forms are derived in the attested languages from a common reconstruction. The two most commonly held hypotheses include (1) derivations related to the Germanic word for 'day' (cf. [cognate set 200](cog-200), not without its own problems in derivation) as *dʰg̑ʰ-i̯es- (zero-grade root + comparative suffix or endingless locative) or (2) a compound of the Indo-European deictic *g̑ʰo- ~ *g̑ʰ- (cf. LIPP 2 275-276) in the zero-grade + the root *dei̯- ~ *di- 'shine' ([NIL](src-274) 69-81, cf. esp. fn6), which underlies words for day in many other branches (cf. [cognate set 375](cog-375)). For a recent extensive discussion of these and other hypotheses, cf. LIPP 2 269-270. For individual branches, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):1692, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):138, [Orel 1998](src-105):68, [EWAia](src-172) II:822, [Abaev 1959–1995](src-156) IV:313-314, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):175-176, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):283, [Matasović 2009](src-50):155). Cf. also [Schindler 1977](src-689) and [Puhvel 1987](src-588) for further discussion on aspects of the IE reconstruction.

Greek, Armenian, and Indo-Iranic lexemes from an original m-stem noun *g̑ʰéi̯-om, *g̑ʰ(i)i̯-ém-, *g̑ʰi-m-´-; based on the ablaut patterns attested among the daughter languages a basic root *g̑ʰei̯- can be abstracted ([NIL](src-274) 162-169, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):1619-1620, [Babinotis 2010](src-382):1599, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):434-435, [EWAia](src-172) II:815-816, [Turner 1962–1966](src-442):815 no. 14096).

Hellenic, Indo-Iranic, Balto-Slavic, and Celtic lexemes derived from PIE *g̑ʰelh₃- 'green, yellow' ([Beekes 2010](src-66):1638, [EWAia](src-172) II:805-806, [ALEW](src-352) 1285-1286, 1296, [Derksen 2015](src-353):511-512, [Derksen 2008](src-81):541, [Matasović 2009](src-50):160).

Because the morphology of the related forms within Greek conform to the Caland system is suggestive that they are inherited from Indo-European, but there are no known cognates outside of Greek (cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):1295-1296, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1672-1673).
Etymology outside of Greek uncertain ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):6, [Beekes 2010](src-66):7), cf. [Pinault 1979](src-717), [Beekes 1996](src-716) for competing hypotheses.

The cognacy of the Greek and Germanic forms is generally agreed, but the derivation of the forms from a common IE proto-form is disputed. An explanation from a compound stem *h₂k-h₂ou̯s-i̯e- 'is sharp-eared' is commonly considered (cf. [Ringe 2006](src-395):71), but this analysis remains uncertain (cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):55). For references to older literature, cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):50-51; [Lehmann 1986](src-179):180-181.

Hellenic, Armenian, and Iranic lexemes derived from PIE *h₂leh₁- 'to grind up' (cf. [LIV²](src-141) 277, [Beekes 2010](src-66):65, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):26-27, [Cheung 2007](src-83):166, [Bailey 1979](src-320):22, [Klingenschmitt 1982](src-558):93).

Hellenic, Armenian, Albanian, Indo-Iranic, and Sabellic lexemes derived from PIE *h₂nér- 'man' ([NIL](src-274) 332-335, cf. The Modern Greek present πεθαίνω was backformed from Ancient/Medieval Greek aorist (ἀ)πέθανον, with replacement of -ανον with present morph. -αίνω and regular loss of initial unstressed ἀ-.

Ancient Greek (ἀπο-)κτείνω 'to kill, put to death', derived from PIE *t⁽k̑⁾én-i̯e/o-, a derivative of the root *t⁽k̑⁾en- 'to injure' ([LIV²](src-141) 645-646, [Beekes 2010](src-66):789-790, cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):591). Wakhi šay- (past stem šit-) has presumably undergone the same semantic narrowing to the meaning 'kill', as against Vedic 'injure' and Avestan 'destroy' ([Morgenstierne 1938](src-334): 543, [Cheung 2007](src-83): 453).

Earlier literature (cf. [Buck 1949](src-47):22) connects Proto-Germanic *samda- [cognate set 284](cog-284), Greek ἄμμος [cognate set 8262](cog-8262), and Lat. sabulum [cognate set 8263](cog-8263) together from an original stem *samdʰo-. This etymology is followed in some recent literature (cf. [Ringe 2006](src-395):11, 101) where the connection between these classes can be maintained through a reconstruction *sámh₂dʰos. On the other hand, Beekes in [EIEC](src-657) objects to this reconstruction on the basis of difficulties within Greek and the necessity to reconstruct IE *a. The Armenian forms in [cognate set 8261](cog-8261) are sometimes also connected to the Germanic, Greek, and Italic ones, but alternative explanations are also possible (cf. [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):149-150). It may well be possible that we are dealing with a European substrate loan into Late-IE which could be accounted for by *samh₂dʰo- (cf. [Kroonen 2013](src-165):426), but the details remain quite unclear. As a consequence of the difficulties in reconciling all the proposed cognacy relations between these four branches, it is preferable to split them into separate cognate sets.

Hellenic, Armenian, Indo-Iranic, Baltic, Germanic, Italic, and Celtic lexemes continuing an inherited word for 'tooth', widely considered to continue a participle *h₁d-ónt- to the verbal root *h₁ed- *'to bite' → 'to eat', lexicalised as 'tooth' already in PIE ([NIL](src-274) 208-220, [LIV²](src-141) 230-231, [EIEC](src-657) 594). Under this explanation the original Ancient Greek form would be continued by Aeolic ἔδοντ-, which underwent vowel assimilation in other dialects. The Leiden School of Indo-European reconstruction alternatively reconstructs a distinct root *h₃ed- 'to bite, sting' following [Kortlandt 2003](src-549):77, who argues that it would better account for ὀδών much more straightforwardly, and it would also much better account for the Ancient Greek privative adjective νωδός 'toothless' < *n̥-h₃d-ó-, (expected †νηδός < *n̥-h₃d-ó-); as for Aeolic ἔδοντ-, it only occurs in late grammatical texts and could have itself been created on the basis of an analogy to Greek ἔδ- 'eat'. For individual branches, cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):776, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1049, [Martirosyan 2010](src-79):1049, [EWAia](src-172) I:693-694, [ALEW](src-352) 174-175, [Derksen 2015](src-353):115, [Ernout & Meillet 1985](src-316):169, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):166-167, [Vendryes et al. 1959–1996](src-296) D:62-63 [Matasović 2009](src-50):90).

gloss: sharp, keen (of a point or edge)
justification: Root etymology disputed. Traditionally to IE *h₂ek̑- 'sharp' (cf. [IEW](src-49) 21-22, [Buck 1949](src-47):1069, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):806-807), but this is difficult from a morphological point of view. Alternatively [Narten 1986](src-722):204-214 has proposed a comparison with Ved. √akṣ- which could allow a Greek zero-grade formation *h₃k̑s- > ὀξ-, but this proposal has not been met with widespread acceptance (cf. The PIE stem is usually reconstructed with initial *h₂- on the basis of Greek ἀστραγαλός 'knucklebone' (cf. [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):129), but the etymological connection of this word to the lexemes in this class is rejected by [Beekes 2010](src-66):157-158 who prefers to see Greek ἀστραγαλός as a substratum loanword.

Connection to a common root *gʷʰreh₁- follows [LIV²](src-141) 221 and [Beekes 2010](src-66):1121, but cf. the reservations of [EWAia](src-172) I:520. For Modern Indic lexemes attached to this set, cf. [Turner 1962–1966](src-442):244, no. 4520, p.245 no. 4531; [KEWA](src-399) I:362. For this Hellenic lexemes in this cognate set, this class encodes the compound element -φραίνομαι.

Two possibilities for a root etymology: Either to *ser- ([LIV²](src-141) 534) or to *u̯er- ([Beekes 2010](src-66):1095-1097, cf. [LIV²](src-141) 3. *u̯er- 'to observe, perceive', [IEW](src-49) 1164).

Generally connected to Lith. vir̃bas 'twig, rod', Rus. верба (OCS връба) 'willow' from a zero-grade fromation *u̯r̥b-, and Lat. uerbera '(rods for) punishment', uerbēnae 'twigs of the laurel' from the full-grade *u̯erb- ([Frisk 1960-1972](src-174) II:636-637, [Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):964), but [Beekes 2010](src-66):1269-1270 is inclined to believe the word is of substratum origin.

Hellenic lexemes, traditionally connected with Baltic lexemes (Lith. ver̃pti, 'spin', Latv. virpêt 'spin with a spindle' ([IEW](src-49) 1156), but the evidence of Myc. e-ra-pe-me-na without initial *w- makes this etymology impossible ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):967, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1275-1276). Further etymology outside of Greek uncertain.

The cognacy of the Hellenic, Germanic, Italic, Celtic, and Albanian lexemes in this set is generally agreed, but the precise root reconstruction is disputed, cf. [Beekes 2010](src-66):1271, 1285, [Vine 1999](src-606):5-30, [Demiraj 1997](src-369):350-351, [Orel 1998](src-105):384, [Holm 2011](src-130):76, [Kroonen 2013](src-165):601, [de Vaan 2008](src-54):512, [Matasović 2009](src-50):430).

Etymology outside of Greek uncertain ([Chantraine 1968–1980](src-270):975, [Beekes 2010](src-66):1287-1288; cf. [IEW](src-49) 1159 for unconvincing older proposals to Germanic lexemes via OHG rīban, etc.).
